language.sample_text: この先工事中 — 注意
language.script_notes: Three scripts mixed together: kanji (dense characters), hiragana (rounded, curved strokes like の/く/し), katakana (angular, for foreign words). Very distinct from Korean Hangul (geometric blocks) or Chinese (kanji only, no hiragana/katakana mixed in).

road_furniture.bollard_color: White with distinctive front/back reflector shapes; regional variation exists.
road_furniture.bollard_shape: Slim posts, often paired at narrow road entrances.
road_furniture.guardrail_type: Simple white guardrail nationwide, with regional colour accents (see regional profiles) — green bands in Kyushu, orange 'natsumikan' guardrails unique to Yamaguchi.
road_furniture.line_paint: White edge and center lines; yellow center line where passing is prohibited, common on narrower roads.
road_furniture.curb_style: Low concrete kerbs, often with a drainage gutter running alongside narrow residential streets.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: Yellow-and-black striped rectangular poles are a strong national tell. Small kanji plates affixed to utility poles name the local area/chōme, useful for narrowing location if legible. Blue road signs with white lettering for directions; yellow diamond warning signs.

architecture.roof_style: Grey ceramic-tiled pitched roofs on traditional houses nationwide; flat/low-slope roofs on urban apartment blocks; heavy snow-load roof shapes in the north.
architecture.roof_material: Grey kawara ceramic tiles are the classic residential roof; corrugated metal on utility/rural buildings.
architecture.wall_construction: Narrow multi-story houses packed tightly on small urban lots; corrugated metal siding common on rural/utility buildings; grey or beige stucco/siding on newer suburban houses.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Muted greys, beiges and browns dominate; utility poles and overhead wires are everywhere and are themselves a strong Japan signal.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Narrow multi-story urban houses wedged onto tiny lots; vending machines on nearly every street corner; konbini (convenience stores — Lawson, 7-Eleven, FamilyMart) with distinctive signage; Shinto torii gates and shrine buildings.

nature.vegetation: Dense cedar/cypress forest covering mountainous terrain nationwide; rice paddies in flat valleys and coastal plains; distinctive broad-leafed 'cabbage-looking' alpine vegetation in Hokkaido and mountainous Honshu.
nature.terrain: Mountainous and forested over most of the country, with development squeezed into narrow coastal plains and valleys; volcanic peaks throughout.
nature.climate_signature: Humid and green most of the year in the south and center; snowy winters with tall snow poles in Hokkaido and the Sea of Japan side of Honshu.

vehicles.plate_color: White plate with green text for private passenger cars, yellow plate with black text for kei (light) cars, green plate with white text for commercial vehicles.
vehicles.plate_format: Two lines — top line: prefecture/city office name in kanji + a classification number; bottom line: one hiragana character + a 2-2 digit serial number.
vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: Boxy kei cars (very small, near-square light vehicles) are a strong Japan tell; Toyota, Honda, Suzuki and Daihatsu dominate the fleet; distinctive white delivery vans and taxis.

google_coverage.camera_generation: Mostly Gen 3 with a growing amount of Gen 4 on recently re-covered roads; clear, sharp, natural-colour imagery.
google_coverage.blur_style: Standard Google blurring, but the camera car itself is mounted lower than normal, producing a distinctly large blurred car/hood in the bottom of frame — this look is shared with only a few other countries (Switzerland, Sri Lanka, some of India).
google_coverage.coverage_notes: Extremely dense, near-complete coverage including narrow residential streets and rural mountain roads.

confusion_set.shared_traits: East Asian urban density, similar utility-pole-and-wire streetscapes, similar vending-machine/convenience-store culture
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Japan drives on the LEFT (Korea drives on the right); Japanese script mixes kanji with rounded hiragana and angular katakana, while Korean uses Hangul's geometric circle/square/line blocks — very different at a glance.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Kanji-derived characters, similar humid subtropical vegetation in the south, dense narrow streets
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Japan drives on the left with yellow-black striped poles and hiragana/katakana mixed in; Taiwan drives on the right with Traditional Chinese only (no hiragana/katakana) and different scooter-dominated street culture.

confusion_set.shared_traits: The distinctive low-mounted camera producing a large blurred car in frame is shared between the two
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Script alone settles it instantly — Japanese kanji/kana vs. Swiss Latin script (German/French/Italian); mountain architecture and road signage are also completely different.
